tasks.short: Track regulatory and technology changes, assess their relevance, and agree changes to search marketing practice.

steps.what: Read regulatory publications and technology guidance, noting relevant changes.

loop.input: New publications from approved sources, with dates, jurisdiction and source links.
loop.output: Source notes containing changes, quoted passages, dates and uncertainty flags.
loop.check: Require a supporting passage for each claim; distinguish proposals, enacted rules and effective dates.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction per publication; unreadable or unsupported items enter a manual queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Feeds and keyword rules retrieve publications, but cannot reliably extract changes from varied prose.

steps.what: Discuss developments with colleagues and attend selected workshops or professional meetings.
Update the change register in {DOCS}, recording sources and follow-up dates.
Compare changes with current tracking, advertising and content practices.

loop.input: Reviewed changes, current marketing controls and campaign inventory.
loop.output: Draft impact assessment linking possible gaps to source passages and affected practices.
loop.check: Strategist checks factual mappings; uncertain legal interpretations are explicitly referred to the compliance lead.
loop.stop: One assessment and one revision per change; missing controls or conflicting sources require human assessment.
loop.why_not_simpler: Applicability depends on the meaning of legal and technical prose and the actual marketing practice.

steps.what: Agree required actions, accountable roles and deadlines with marketing and compliance colleagues.
Send the approved action plan through {EMAIL} and request progress updates.

tasks.design: A scheduled flow in {WORKFLOW} collects approved publications from {GOV_PORTAL} and {DOCS}, removes duplicates and creates source-linked change notes through a bounded reading loop. A second bounded loop drafts impact assessments against documented marketing controls; people agree actions, while {WORKFLOW} maintains the register and sends reminders through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources were scattered, applicability required reading, and maintaining a reliable register brought little immediate campaign benefit.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing feeds, document extraction and configurable records handle collection and tracking. Bounded text extraction can reduce reading time, while AI-assisted coding can make small source adapters cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Source coverage, changing effective dates and legal applicability still need specialist judgement. GDPR and the EU AI Act apply where relevant; national rules determine consultation requirements for changes affecting employees.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising which change matters commercially, questioning a confident interpretation and learning through trusted professional relationships.

ambition.what: A source-linked marketing change clinic for campaign owners.

tasks.altitude: The strategist spends less time maintaining reading lists and more time testing how changes affect campaigns. They can prioritise the clinic agenda; legal interpretation and control approval remain with the compliance lead.

reach.task: Prepare a briefing on how regulatory changes affect public claims.
reach.learn: Separate binding requirements from commentary and explain uncertainty without overstating it.

evidence.claim: Source collection, duplicate removal, dated registers and reminders can use deterministic automation.
Source-linked extraction can assist reading, but applicability assessment needs human judgement.
The digest documents a report containing nonexistent citations, supporting explicit source checks for generated briefings.

assumptions: The initial scope covers a defined set of marketing practices, jurisdictions and approved sources.
Build ranges are working-day estimates for a pilot, not measured delivery results or elapsed-time guarantees.
Consultation effort covers checking national rules and completing applicable consultation; substantial negotiation could extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which sources, jurisdictions and languages the team must cover.
Whether marketing controls and campaign inventories are documented and current.
Who approves legal interpretations and remediation priorities.
Which access permissions and employee consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Which authoritative sources provide stable feeds, version histories and effective-date metadata?
How accurately can extraction distinguish proposals from rules in force across the required languages?
new_work: Review extracted changes and resolve ambiguous applicability.
Maintain the source list and repair failed collection routes.
Keep marketing controls current and close completed actions.
Check a sample of summaries against original publications.

tasks.short: Choose, negotiate and purchase local search listings, then verify publication and charges.

steps.what: Inspect existing listings and placement options in {PARTNER_PORTAL}.
Compare coverage, fees, terms and historical results in {SPREADSHEET}.
Negotiate price, placement, cancellation terms and reporting with the listing provider.
Enter the negotiated offer and supporting details into {PROCUREMENT}.
Approve placement spend and terms in {PROCUREMENT}.
Submit the purchase and listing details through {PARTNER_PORTAL}.
Check published listing fields and placement dates in {PARTNER_PORTAL}.
Match the supplier invoice against the approved purchase in {ERP}.

tasks.design: A listing register in {WORKFLOW} combines authorised data from {PARTNER_PORTAL}, the location master and performance data in {BI}; deterministic comparisons prepare the shortlist and purchase request in {PROCUREMENT}. People negotiate and approve spend, then review the exact submission before an integration purchases the placement; verification results support invoice matching in {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Listing providers used different fields and access methods, while low purchase volumes rarely justified bespoke integrations.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable field mappings, existing approval flows and faster adapter development make a limited provider set practical. Comparison and submission do not require a model when inputs are structured.
tasks.still_hard: Provider access, location ownership verification, nonstandard terms and uncertain incremental value remain difficult. GDPR applies where listings contain personal contact details; contractual commitments need clear authority.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiating concessions, judging provider credibility and deciding whether a placement deserves budget despite imperfect attribution.

ambition.what: A managed local-listing service for small branch teams without dedicated marketing staff.

tasks.altitude: The strategist spends more time negotiating useful placements and helping branch teams choose coverage. They gain control of branch onboarding priorities; spending approval stays with the marketing manager.

reach.task: Evaluate a proposed regional placement package.
reach.learn: Assess incremental reach, cancellation exposure and evidence of commercial return.

evidence.claim: Structured listing comparisons, approval routing and invoice matching can use deterministic rules.
Provider-specific submission and verification depend on supported access and cannot be assumed from the task description.

assumptions: The pilot covers a small set of providers with authorised structured access or supported file submission.
The location master and approved listing copy already exist.
Negotiated offers are recorded in structured fields before purchase-request creation.
Build ranges include access review and checking whether national employee consultation rules apply; no employee monitoring is proposed.
unknowns: Which providers offer supported read and write access.
Whether purchases are self-service, negotiated or arranged through an intermediary.
Who may accept terms, commit spend and approve listing content.
How location verification and supplier onboarding work.
Whether existing invoice matching can use listing verification.
research_questions: Which provider interfaces support idempotent purchasing, status retrieval and listing comparison?
What measurement design can separate placement effects from existing local demand?
new_work: Maintain provider mappings and handle rejected submissions.
Resolve location ownership and listing discrepancies.
Review exact purchase payloads and retain approval records.
Investigate invoice mismatches and duplicate purchases.

tasks.short: Align merchandising, stock and search intent so product catalogues stay accurate and easy to find.

steps.what: Export current product records from {ECOMMERCE}.
Export stock availability and replenishment constraints from {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Export query performance from search reporting in {OTHER}.
Join exports in {SPREADSHEET} and flag missing fields, stale availability and unmatched queries.
Propose query-to-category mappings, labels and catalogue priorities in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Unmatched queries, existing taxonomy, verified product attributes and promotion calendar.
loop.output: Proposed category mappings and labels, with supporting queries and ambiguity flags.
loop.check: Use exact and synonym matches first; validate category identifiers and product attributes; review novel mappings.
loop.stop: One classification and one correction per query batch; unresolved intent goes to the planning meeting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules cover established mappings, but ambiguous language and new query intent require semantic interpretation.

steps.what: Agree catalogue priorities with merchandising, operations and inventory colleagues.
Prepare product and category edits as drafts in {ECOMMERCE}.
Approve exact catalogue changes in {ECOMMERCE}.
Publish the approved catalogue version in {ECOMMERCE}.

tasks.design: Scheduled exports from {ECOMMERCE}, {OPS_SYSTEM} and search reporting in {OTHER} feed deterministic quality checks on {DATA_PLATFORM}. Exact and synonym rules handle known queries; a bounded classification loop proposes unfamiliar mappings for joint planning, and {ECOMMERCE} publishes only the exact draft version approved by the merchandising manager.
tasks.previous_blocker: Product identifiers, stock timing and query language did not align, so people reconciled exports and negotiated priorities by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports and draft publication controls cover much of the work. Small joins and validation checks are cheaper to build, with a bounded language loop reserved for unfamiliar query intent.
tasks.still_hard: Stock freshness, variant identifiers and commercial trade-offs remain expensive to resolve. Product claims must remain supported; GDPR applies if query exports contain personal data.
tasks.human_edge: Balancing customer intent with stock constraints, margins and merchandising commitments, especially when teams want different priorities.

ambition.what: A weekly decision on which in-stock category should receive the next findability improvement.

tasks.altitude: Reconciliation takes less of the week, leaving time for category experiments with the online merchant. The strategist can sequence approved findability tests; merchandising retains product and assortment approval.

reach.learn: Understand product variants, stock latency, commercial guardrails and catalogue publication controls.

reach.task: Test whether category labels help customers find products.
reach.learn: Use task-based usability evidence alongside search and conversion data.

evidence.claim: Identifier joins, field validation, stock checks and version-bound publication can use deterministic technology.
Ambiguous queries can benefit from bounded semantic classification, with human review of new mappings.

assumptions: This task applies to an organisation with a product catalogue and a distinct inventory source.
Stable product identifiers and authorised exports are available.
The pilot changes labels, mappings and approved attributes rather than inventing product claims.
Build ranges cover a limited catalogue pilot, access review and applicable national consultation checks.
unknowns: Whether product identifiers match across {ECOMMERCE} and {OPS_SYSTEM}.
How fresh stock data must be before a promotion or publication.
Whether {ECOMMERCE} supports drafts, version-bound approval and rollback.
Which query fields contain personal data and what use is permitted.
Who can approve taxonomy, claims and live catalogue changes.
research_questions: Which query patterns are reliably handled by synonyms before semantic classification is needed?
What experiment can distinguish findability improvements from stock and promotion effects?
new_work: Resolve unmatched product identifiers and stale stock feeds.
Review ambiguous query mappings and maintain approved synonyms.
Check draft differences and invalidate approvals after edits.
Investigate failed publication and maintain rollback procedures.
Evaluate category experiments with merchandising colleagues.

tasks.short: Run social campaigns and use their results to choose better search marketing tests.

steps.what: Define the campaign hypothesis, audience, message and search learning objective in {DOCS}.
Export audience and campaign results from {SOCIAL}.
Draft posts and assemble approved creative assets in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Campaign brief, approved claims, existing creative assets and aggregated performance findings.
loop.output: Post variants linked to approved claims and asset identifiers.
loop.check: Validate links, length limits and asset rights; reviewer checks factual support, tone and suitability.
loop.stop: At most three variants per brief and one revision; unsupported claims or missing assets return to the strategist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates assemble assets, but useful message variants require writing suited to the hypothesis and audience.

steps.what: Review content and approve the publication schedule through {EMAIL}.
Schedule approved posts in {SOCIAL}.
Approve paid audience settings, campaign dates and spend limits in {ADS}.
Activate the approved paid campaign in {ADS}.
Check delivery, spend and engagement against campaign targets in {BI}.
Discuss findings and choose the next search hypothesis to test.

tasks.design: A brief form in {WORKFLOW} assembles approved claims and assets from {DOCS}, and a bounded writing loop prepares post variants for content approval. Existing scheduling and spend controls in {SOCIAL} and {ADS} execute only version-bound approved content and campaign settings; deterministic feeds into {BI} support the strategist's next search experiment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Briefs, approvals, creative assets and performance reports were disconnected, while interpreting social response still required marketing judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling, approval and reporting features cover most execution. Small integrations can connect the records, with a bounded writing loop reducing repetitive drafting.
tasks.still_hard: Social engagement does not establish search intent or incremental sales. Audience data use must comply with GDPR, and EU AI Act obligations must be assessed for the actual use, including any applicable content transparency duties.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a meaningful hypothesis, judging tone and distinguishing a promising customer insight from an engagement spike.

ambition.what: A weekly choice of the next search message experiment informed by social campaign results.

tasks.altitude: Less scheduling and report assembly leaves more time for experiment design with the marketing manager. The strategist gains control of test sequencing within approved campaigns; new spend and audience changes retain manager approval.

reach.task: Design a comparison that tests whether a message changes customer response.
reach.learn: Control confounding factors, set sample requirements and distinguish exploratory signals from causal evidence.

reach.task: Review campaign messages for reputational sensitivity.
reach.learn: Recognise context-dependent tone, claim risks and situations requiring escalation.

evidence.claim: Scheduling, campaign limits, approval routing and aggregated reporting commonly use configurable deterministic features.
Bounded drafting from approved material can reduce preparation work while preserving content and spend approvals.
Social engagement alone cannot establish a causal effect on search outcomes.

assumptions: The strategist coordinates campaign execution with access to approved creative assets.
Paid activation applies only to campaigns that include paid distribution.
Reporting initially uses aggregated data rather than individual-level cross-channel matching.
Content edits or audience and budget changes invalidate the relevant approval.
Build ranges include access review, applicable national consultation checks and a limited campaign pilot.
unknowns: Which scheduling, approval and budget controls are already configured.
Who approves claims, creative assets, audience settings and spend.
Whether the available data can connect social activity with meaningful search outcomes.
What lawful audience data use and asset permissions have been established.
Whether the strategist has delegated authority to sequence tests within approved campaigns.
research_questions: Which aggregated measures provide useful early signals for search experiments?
Which experiment design can separate message effects from audience and distribution changes?
Which native approval features bind publication and activation to an exact approved version?
new_work: Review generated variants and maintain approved claims and asset permissions.
Handle rejected posts, broken links and failed campaign activation.
Maintain metric definitions and investigate tracking gaps.
Review alerts and decide whether a campaign needs intervention.
Record experiment results and retire unsupported hypotheses.

role.altitude: The week shifts from collecting updates, reconciling exports and arranging publication toward experiments, commercial negotiation and cross-team decisions. The target role gains control of experiment sequencing and service priorities within approved plans; legal, product and spending approvals remain with the relevant roles.
reach: Support branch teams with local-listing choices and onboarding.
Work with the online merchant on stock-aware category experiments.
Work with a market research analyst on credible cross-channel tests.
Help public relations colleagues interpret marketing changes and message risks.
skills_to_grow: Product identifiers, taxonomy and data quality.
Source verification and practical regulatory interpretation.
Approval design, exception handling and integration monitoring.
role.ambitious_version: Run a search learning programme that turns verified regulatory updates, catalogue gaps and social campaign findings into prioritised experiments, while offering branch teams a managed local-listing service.
